fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Water Feature; Access Drive; Dense Vegetation; Walkway
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Water Feature; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responders arriving under low-visibility conditions can locate it quickly.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so fire and emergency apparatus can reach both structures without obstruction.
• Create a designated turnaround area near the residence or detached structure so apparatus can exit without backing the full length of the access drive.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain clearance for emergency vehicles at mirror height and above.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the main residence and detached structure so responders can move around both buildings without obstruction.
• Keep a clear walking path between the main residence and detached structure so responders can move quickly between the two.
• Mark the water feature with a visible indicator so responders working in low-light or smoke conditions are aware of its location and edge.
• Install reflective markers or paint along the edge of the water feature closest to the access drive and walkways to prevent responders from stepping into it during nighttime or emergency operations.
• Keep walkways clear of furniture, planters, or landscaping materials so responders can move quickly around the property on foot.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Tree Cluster; Open Green Space; Scattered Trees; Water Feature; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Vegetation Along Driveway; Scattered Shrubs; Limited Rear Access; Single Access Route
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure to create open space between individual trees and between the trees and the house.
• Trim branches on large trees that extend over or close to the roofline and walls of the structure.
• Remove or cut back shrubs growing directly against the structure on all sides.
• Clear dead leaves, fallen branches, and loose plant material from around the base of trees near the house.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway so vehicles, including fire trucks, can pass through without obstruction.
• Cut back shrubs and low branches along the driveway edges to keep the travel lane open and visible.
• Clear vegetation along the rear of the property to open a path for movement around the back of the structure.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from scattered shrubs near the structure and any outbuildings.
• Keep the area between the tree clusters and the structure free of shrubs, debris, and low-hanging branches that could connect fire from one to the other.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate and navigate, particularly given the single access route to the property.
• Keep the single access route clear of fallen branches, overgrown vegetation, and any debris that could block or slow entry.
